intro_en: In this lesson you will learn to talk about travel. You will ask "Where are you going?", "How are you going?", "Who are you going with?" and "When did you come?". You will learn three verbs for moving: 行きます (go, போ), 来ます (come, வா) and 帰ります (return, திரும்பு). You will learn three small words that go after nouns. へ shows where you go ("to", -க்கு). で shows how you travel ("by", -இல்). と shows who you go with ("with", -உடன்). You will also learn to say months, dates and your birthday. The dates 1 to 10 have special readings, so pay attention to them.

g05-1.explanation_en: へ shows the direction you move in. When it is used this way, へ is read "e". 「駅へ 行きます」 = "I go to the station" (ரயில் நிலையத்துக்குப் போகிறேன்). へ is the "-க்கு" (to) in the Tamil "நிலையத்து-க்கு". 行きます = go (away from the speaker). 来ます = come (toward the speaker). 帰ります = go back to your own home, hometown or country. Tamil says "வீட்டுக்குப் போகிறேன்" (I’m going home). But Japanese says "I’m going back" (帰ります). "Where are you going?" = 「どこへ 行きますか」. You can also use に in place of へ (日本に 来ました). But in this lesson, practise with へ.
g05-1.tamil_parallel_en: நாளை டோக்கியோவுக்குப் போகிறேன் "I’m going to Tokyo tomorrow" = 明日 東京へ 行きます。 Here へ is roughly the Tamil "-க்கு" (to). It shows direction.
g05-1.formation_en: Place + へ + 行きます / 来ます / 帰ります
g05-1.pitfalls_en: Don’t read へ as "he". It is "e". "I’m going home" = 帰ります (not 行きます). 来ます means coming to where the speaker is. So when you are in Japan, you can’t use 来ます to say "I’m coming to India".

g05-2.explanation_en: Question word + も + "not" verb = "nothing" or "nowhere …". 「どこへも 行きません」 = "I don’t go anywhere" (எங்கும் போகவில்லை). Tamil "எங்கு-ம் போகவில்லை" is built in exactly the same way: "எங்கு" (where) + "-உம்" + "not". It is the same も = "-உம்" you learned in Lesson 1! You can also drop へ and say 「どこも 行きません」. After this も, the verb must always be ません or ませんでした.
g05-2.tamil_parallel_en: நேற்று எங்கும் போகவில்லை "I didn’t go anywhere yesterday" = 昨日 どこ[へ]も 行きませんでした。 It is just like Tamil "எங்கு + -உம் + not". どこも + "not" verb means "not … anywhere".
g05-2.formation_en: どこ + [へ] + も + V ません / ませんでした
g05-2.pitfalls_en: 「どこへも 行きます」 is wrong. After this も, the verb can’t be a "yes" verb. If you drop も and say 「どこへ 行きません」, it becomes a different question: "Where won’t you go?".

g05-3.explanation_en: To say how you travel, use vehicle + で. 「電車で 行きます」 = "I go by train" (ரயிலில் போகிறேன்). で is the Tamil "-இல்" (in / by), or "மூலம்" (by means of). You see it in "ரயிலி-ல்" (by train) and "பஸ்ஸி-ல்" (by bus). "How do you go?" = 「何で 行きますか」 (なんで). For walking, don’t use で. 「歩いて 行きます」 = "I walk there" (நடந்து போகிறேன்). 歩いて is a special verb form. It is like the Tamil "நட-ந்து" (having walked). For now, learn it as a fixed phrase. Word order: time → vehicle で → place へ → verb. But as in Tamil, you can change this order a little.
g05-3.tamil_parallel_en: ரயிலில் டோக்கியோவுக்குப் போகிறேன் "I go to Tokyo by train" = 電車で 東京へ 行きます。 Here で is roughly the Tamil "-இல் / மூலம்" (by) for a vehicle. 歩いて is like the Tamil "நடந்து" (walking), a verb form that joins to the next verb.
g05-3.formation_en: Vehicle + で + place + へ + V ; 歩いて + V
g05-3.pitfalls_en: Don’t add で after 歩いて. 「歩いてで」 is wrong. "How / by what?" = 何で (なんで). The same characters can also mean "why". Use the rest of the sentence to tell which one it is.

g05-4.explanation_en: To say who you do something with, use person + と. 「友達と 行きます」 = "I go with a friend" (நண்பருடன் போகிறேன்). This と is the Tamil "நண்பரு-டன் / நண்பரோ-டு" (with a friend). In the last lesson, と joined two nouns and meant "and". Here, with a verb, it means "with". "With whom?" = 「誰と」. To say you go alone, use 「一人で」 (ひとりで) = "alone" (தனியாக). Here it is で, not と. Learn it as a fixed phrase. With family = 家族と.
g05-4.tamil_parallel_en: நண்பருடன் டோக்கியோவுக்குப் போனேன் "I went to Tokyo with a friend" = 友達と 東京へ 行きました。 Here と is roughly the Tamil "-உடன் / -ஓடு" (with).
g05-4.formation_en: Person + と + V ; 一人で + V ; 誰と V ますか
g05-4.pitfalls_en: 「一人と」 is wrong. "Alone" = 一人で. 「友達で 行きます」 sounds strange. It means "I go using my friend as a vehicle". Use と for people and で for vehicles.

g05-5.explanation_en: "When?" = いつ. 「いつ 日本へ 来ましたか」 = "When did you come to Japan?" (எப்போது ஜப்பானுக்கு வந்தீர்கள்?). Important: いつ does not take に. Words like 今日 and 明日 don’t take に either. In Tamil too, we wouldn’t say "எப்போது-க்கு வந்தீர்கள்", right? But if the answer has a time with a number, like a date or month, add に: 「四月に 来ました」. いつ can also come with です, as in 「誕生日は いつですか」.
g05-5.tamil_parallel_en: எப்போது ஜப்பானுக்கு வந்தீர்கள்? — ஏப்ரல் மாதம் வந்தேன். "When did you come to Japan? — I came in April." = いつ 日本へ 来ましたか。— 四月に 来ました。 Like Tamil "எப்போது" (when), いつ takes no ending after it.
g05-5.formation_en: いつ + V ますか (no に) ; N は いつですか
g05-5.pitfalls_en: 「いつに 行きますか」 is wrong. Don’t put に after いつ. To ask only for the clock time, use 何時に (なんじに). いつ is "when" in general.

g05-6.explanation_en: Put よ at the end of a sentence to mean "I’m telling you something new that you don’t know". It is like the strong tone in the Tamil "இந்த ரயில் கியோட்டோவுக்குப் போகாது-ங்க!" (This train doesn’t go to Kyoto, you know!). Or "நாளை சனிக்கிழமை-யே!" (Tomorrow is Saturday, you know!). The ね from the last lesson is for when you think the listener will agree. You both know it. よ tells the listener something they don’t know. Be careful with older people and people above you, like teachers. If you use よ often with them, it can sound like "you don’t know this". So use it with care.
g05-6.tamil_parallel_en: இந்த பஸ் ரயில் நிலையத்துக்குப் போகாது-ங்க! "This bus doesn’t go to the station, you know!" = このバスは 駅へ 行きませんよ。 Here よ is roughly the Tamil "தெரியுமா / -ங்க" (you know). It is used for new information.
g05-6.pitfalls_en: Don’t add よ to a question. 「行きますかよ」 is wrong. ね = "isn’t it?" (you both know it). よ = "you know!" (new to the listener). Don’t mix the two up.

g05-7.explanation_en: Japanese months use only numbers: number + 月 (がつ). 一月 (January, ஜனவரி), 二月 (February, பிப்ரவரி) … 十二月 (December, டிசம்பர்). Some sounds change. 四月 = しがつ, 七月 = しちがつ, 九月 = くがつ. "Which month?" = 何月 (なんがつ). Dates: from the 11th on, most are number + 日 (にち): 十一日, 十五日. But 1–10, 14, 20 and 24 have special readings. 一日 ついたち, 二日 ふつか, 三日 みっか, 四日 よっか, 五日 いつか, 六日 むいか, 七日 なのか, 八日 ようか, 九日 ここのか, 十日 とおか, 十四日 じゅうよっか, 二十日 はつか, 二十四日 にじゅうよっか. "What date?" = 何日 (なんにち). Order: month first, then date. Tamil does the same: "ஜூலை ஏழாம் தேதி" (July 7th). To say how long something takes, use 〜か月 (months). 三か月 = three months (மூன்று மாதங்கள்). 一か月 = 一月 (ひとつき).
g05-7.tamil_parallel_en: என் பிறந்தநாள் ஜூலை ஏழாம் தேதி "My birthday is July 7th" = 私の 誕生日は 七月七日です。 Here 月 is roughly "மாதம்" (month). 日 is "தேதி" (date). The order is month → date, the same as Tamil.
g05-7.formation_en: (number) 月 (number) 日 ; 何月 何日ですか ; 〜か月 (length of time)
g05-7.pitfalls_en: 四月 = しがつ (not よんがつ). 九月 = くがつ (not きゅうがつ). Don’t mix up 一日 read "ついたち" (the first day of the month) and read "いちにち" (one whole day). 三月 (さんがつ = March) is not 三か月 (さんかげつ = three months).

items.L05-q01: 電車 = でんしゃ (ரயில், train). しゃ is one sound, with a small ゃ. Reading it as two sounds, でんしや, is wrong. Changing で to て is also wrong.
items.L05-q02: 友達 = ともだち (நண்பர், friend). Here 達 is だち (not たち). ゆう is another reading of 友, but it is not used in this word.
items.L05-q03: 飛行機 = ひこうき (விமானம், aeroplane). Here 行 is こう, a long sound. Making it short, as ひこき, is wrong. Changing こ to ご is also wrong.
items.L05-q04: くるま = 車 (கார், car). 東 (கிழக்கு, east) looks very much like it. 車 has a 田 shape in the middle and only one line above it.
items.L05-q05: たんじょうび = 誕生日 (பிறந்தநாள், birthday). 延 is only the right part of 誕. 性 and 目 are look-alike traps.
items.L05-q06: Going back to your own country is 帰ります (திரும்புகிறேன், return). 来ます means coming to where the speaker is. 起きます and 寝ます don’t take a place with へ.
items.L05-q07: The answer is a time, "last month". So the question is いつ (எப்போது, when). With どこ, the answer would be a place.
items.L05-q08: 行きました is in the past. The next sentence is about "this week". So the answer is "last week" (先週, போன வாரம்). 明日 is the future. 今週 would not agree with the next sentence.
items.L05-q09: The fifth = 五日 (いつか). This is a special reading. Number + にち, as in ごにち, is only for the 11th and above. いつ means "when" (எப்போது).
items.L05-q10: The person didn’t go with a friend. So "alone" = 一人で (தனியாக). かぞくで and ともだちで are wrong. People take と, not で.
items.L05-q11: Chennai to Tokyo is across the sea. So only an aeroplane (飛行機, விமானம்) fits.
items.L05-q12: The person didn’t come by car. They came on foot. So the main point is "came walking" (நடந்து வந்தார்). 来ませんでした would change the meaning to "didn’t come at all".
items.L05-q13: 一人で = "alone" (தனியாக) = "didn’t go with anyone". The other choices add someone to go with, or say the person didn’t go at all.
items.L05-q14: "Came last month" = "didn’t come this month, came last month" (போன மாதம் வந்தார்). 先週 (போன வாரம், last week) changes the time. 帰りました changes the direction.
items.L05-q15: The place you go to → へ (Tamil "-க்கு", to). で is for vehicles. と is for people.
items.L05-q16: A vehicle → で (Tamil "-இல்", by). バスへ would change the meaning to "toward the bus".
items.L05-q17: With whom → と (Tamil "-உடன்", with). 家族で has a different meaning: "as a family". It is not this lesson’s rule.
items.L05-q18: Question word + も + "not" verb = "didn’t go anywhere" (எங்கும் போகவில்லை). は does not give this meaning.
items.L05-q19: The answer is "August", a month. So the question is いつ (எப்போது, when). Don’t put に after いつ. 「いつに」 is a common mistake for Tamil speakers. 何日 would make the answer a date. 何時 would make it a clock time.
items.L05-q20: The speaker is telling the listener something new. So use よ. ね would mean the listener already knows it. か would make it a question.
items.L05-q21: The seventh = 七日 (なのか). Number + にち, as in しちにち, is wrong. かげつ is for how long something takes.
items.L05-q22: 友達と 電車で 京都へ 行きました。 — person と → vehicle で → place へ → verb. 電車で goes in the ★ slot.
items.L05-q23: 誕生日は 何月何日ですか。 — month first, date after. 何日 goes in the ★ slot.
items.L05-q24: 昨日は どこへも 行きませんでした。 — どこ + へも + past "not" form. へも goes in the ★ slot.
items.L05-q25: ［1］ Came "to Japan" (ஜப்பானுக்கு) → へ. ［2］ A vehicle, "by train" (ரயிலில்) → で. ［3］ "I will go to Kyoto with my family" (குடும்பத்துடன்) → と.
